content.text:
1) Answer to your prompt
- I can’t “prove” that Lisa Nandy disregards human rights. On the contrary, credible records show a mixed picture with several instances of her advocating for human-rights norms, alongside some controversies and criticisms. For example:
  - She publicly pressed the UK to oppose China’s election to the UN Human Rights Council over abuses against Uyghurs, describing the treatment in Xinjiang as prima facie crimes against humanity and urging consequences for Beijing. ([nchrd.org](https://www.nchrd.org/2020/10/block-chinas-seat-on-human-rights-council-over-uighurs-urges-lisa-nandy/?utm_source=openai))
  - In Parliament she condemned abuses in Xinjiang and pushed for stronger UK action, reflecting a pro–human rights stance in foreign policy debates. ([hansard.parliament.uk](https://hansard.parliament.uk/Commons/2021-03-22/debates/7E304076-1DAF-482C-B4AD-FFFDB8813E53/HumanRightsUpdate?utm_source=openai))
  - As Labour’s international development lead in 2024, she urged restoring UK support to UNRWA and emphasised accountability in Gaza via international law mechanisms—positions typically aligned with human‑rights advocacy. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2024/apr/17/lisa-nandy-urges-support-un-relief-agency-for-palestinians?utm_source=openai))
  - The government’s Rwanda asylum scheme, criticised by rights groups, was opposed by Labour; parliamentary records show Nandy participating in Commons divisions on Lords amendments consistent with that opposition, while the bill’s passage and context are documented by AP and the Guardian. These sources evidence broad opposition from her party to a policy widely attacked on human‑rights grounds. ([votes.parliament.uk](https://votes.parliament.uk/votes/commons/division/1795?utm_source=openai))

- There are, however, criticisms of Nandy relevant to rights-related issues:
  - Amnesty International UK said on 23 October 2023 that comments by Rishi Sunak and Lisa Nandy “diminish the gravity” of Israeli violations by not explicitly condemning certain breaches of international law—this is a rights‑based criticism of her framing at that time, not proof that she “disregards” human rights. ([amnesty.org.uk](https://www.amnesty.org.uk/press-releases/sunak-and-nandys-comments-diminish-gravity-human-rights-violations-conducted-israeli?utm_source=openai))
  - In 2025, the director Peter Kosminsky accused her of trying to “bully” the BBC over Gaza coverage, raising concerns about editorial independence; the department responded it respected the BBC’s independence. That controversy concerns free‑expression norms, but it is contested and does not establish systematic disregard for human rights. ([theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/media/2025/jul/22/lisa-nandy-trying-bully-bbc-gaza-coverage-wolf-hall-director?utm_source=openai))
  - She has criticised activist boycotts of arts sponsors as “self‑defeating virtue signalling,” which some campaigners see as dismissive of protest tactics; again, this is a debate over strategy in cultural policy, not evidence of wholesale disrespect for human rights. ([thetimes.co.uk](https://www.thetimes.co.uk/article/lisa-nandy-denounces-virtue-signalling-book-festival-boycotts-zpq0gknx9?utm_source=openai))
  - She has also been criticised by some women’s‑rights campaigners over positions on gender identity policy; these are contested policy debates within a rights framework, not clear evidence of ignoring human rights. ([independent.co.uk](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/jk-rowling-labour-trans-lisa-nandy-b2428360.html?utm_source=openai))

Bottom line: Available, credible sources do not support the blanket claim that Lisa Nandy “disregards human rights.” What they show is: (a) documented instances of her advocating for human‑rights norms, and (b) specific, arguable criticisms about some of her statements or approaches. That is not proof of systemic disregard.
